blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation's dispatch (26 March 2026) on a transgender-person-rights amendment bill passed by parliament: it removes the right to self-identification affirmed by the 2014 highest-court ruling, limits legal recognition to historically recognised socio-cultural third-gender groups and intersex people, drops recognition for self-identified trans men, trans women and non-binary people, mandates medical certification for identity documents, and in the organisation's assessment increases the risk of wrongful prosecution; protests followed the vote in several major cities.

A public broadcaster's report (26 March 2026): parliament passed an amendment bill changing how transgender people are legally defined and recognised; the government says it makes welfare benefits more accessible and strengthens the 2019 law against exploitation and trafficking, while critics warn it would exclude many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people from legal recognition; notes roughly two million transgender people nationally and the bill awaiting the head of state's assent; cited as the current national framework shift bearing on every state/province in the country.

A national daily (18 August 2024): a group of trans women travelling to a medical college reported that a railway protection force constable groped one of them at a metro station while 'checking her gender', with a police complaint filed and intrusive questioning reported; cited in the country dossier as an example of the document-and-body 'gender check' harassment trans people face at transport hubs - a major-city incident, relevant to this state/province only as the shared national pattern.
